text:
maya: seeing a regression in tail latency on prod after the last runtime canary. small requests (<=80 tokens) show queue-time dominated tails. attaching nsys/perfetto traces, but can anyone eyeball this quickly?

sam: looking now. quick glance at trace: kvcache sweep bursts line up with queue spikes. also some host->GPU memcpy spikes during the same windows.

li: fwiw the kernel selector fell back to non-fused matmul on SM80 for this model in the canary trace. matmul_plain launch count jumped compared to baseline. suspect padded seq_len/prefetch mismatch.

ana: i repro locally with perfetto. toggling continuous_batch_window lowers tail a lot. pushed a small change toggling preemptive_affinity heuristic to test. perf diff below.

```
before: p50 18ms  p95 72ms
after:  p50 17ms  p95 39ms
```

ryan: can we check if the prefetch policy is causing extra kvcache sweeps? can someone dump /metrics/kvcache/sweep_count for the period?

sam: attaching quick metrics dump — sweep_count clearly spikes concurrent with long queues. also host CPU scheduling jitter visible. snippet: 

```
2026-03-13T12:15:32Z kvcache.sweep=0
2026-03-13T12:15:34Z kvcache.sweep=3
2026-03-13T12:15:36Z kvcache.sweep=0
```

jon: nsys flame snapshot: matmul_plain takes ~35% GPU time and there are repeated relaunches (3x) for the same request due to small-window preemption. kernel launch overhead + smaller effective batch = worse throughput and tail.

maya: working hypothesis: when continuous_batch_window is shorter than kernel_launch_latency we end up preempting batches or fragmenting them. that increases number of kernel launches and can trigger selector to choose fallback kernels (shape/padding reasons). result = longer compute per token + increased queue backlog. needs a runtime fix: prefer kernel affinity by sequence_len bin and avoid preemption for pending batches smaller than threshold X.

li: agree. i'll open a PR that pins kernel affinity at batch-slot granularity and adds hysteresis to the preemptive scheduler so it won't preempt if remaining window < kernel_launch_latency * factor. will include microbench unit test.

ana: i'll add canary dashboards for kvcache_sweep_rate and kernel_relaunches/min so we can detect regressions quickly. also will run an A/B with continuous_batch_window 3ms vs 7ms on canary.

sam: next steps on traces: run full nsys with host CPU tracing + perfetto timeline, and include nvlink/memcpy markers. command I used locally: 

```
nsys profile -o out --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=none --stats true --force-overwrite --kill=5 --nvtx=true -- ./bin/infer --profile-mode=canary
```

ryan: i'll run nsys on prod-canary and collect host runqueue + top CPU syscalls. also collect kernel selection debug logs (selector.v=2) for the same window.

maya: thanks. To summarize assignments: @li -> PR for kernel-affinity+scheduler hysteresis, @ana -> canary dashboards + A/B runs, @ryan -> nsys on canary, @sam -> collect full perf traces and metrics correlation. i'll follow up with a short postmortem if this lands in baseline. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout r2026.3 scheduled to canary cluster infer-prod-east-1 at 2026-03-14T07:00:00Z.
